page: Microsoft Azure FX24-6mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration belonging to the FXmdsv2 series, engineered for memory-intensive enterprise computing requiring elevated per-core compute capacity. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 6 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 3 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz with 260 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning is notably high, delivering 504 GB of RAM, or 84 GB per core. The host includes 1416 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with Premium Storage capability, while omitting GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations reflect the architectural profile of the instance. In Geekbench single-core evaluations, the server achieves top-tier results with a score of 2362.0, mirrored by top-decile text processing throughput at 2948.0. Compression benchmarks also exhibit strong performance, with single-threaded gzip compression reaching 34.83 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 14.37 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics—such as a multi-core Geekbench score of 7259.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12058.01—register within the middle 50% of tested systems due to the constrained physical core count. While AMX and AVX-512 extensions aid vectorized calculations, CPU-bound LLM text generation remains modest, delivering 4.59 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The hardware configuration provides strong cost efficiency for software with licensing models tied to CPU core counts, maximizing available memory and I/O per licensed core. The integration of a 1416 GB NVMe disk delivers fast scratch storage without relying solely on remote network disks. The primary engineering tradeoff is the low overall multi-threaded parallel throughput relative to the substantial memory footprint. As a result, the instance is best suited for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines that depend heavily on single-thread execution speed.
description: Microsoft Azure FX24-6mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine designed for compute and memory-intensive workloads requiring high single-core performance. Driven by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz across 6 vCPUs (3 physical cores), the system provides an exceptional memory footprint of 504 GB, resulting in 84 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration features include AVX-512, AMX matrix extensions, and cryptographic instruction sets. Storage needs are met by an integrated 1416 GB local NVMe SSD with Premium Storage support, though no GPU acceleration is present. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-core execution, achieving 2362.0 on Geekbench single-core and strong throughput in compression routines, while multi-core and large-model inference metrics reflect its modest physical core count. The instance offers resource efficiency for per-core licensed enterprise databases, electronic design automation, financial analytics, and memory-heavy workloads with limited parallel threading requirements.
